errors.text_span: Figure 10 illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, with error bars indicating the standard deviation.
errors.evidence: The chart does not illustrate the effect of context masking on case tasks; it shows the effect on different language families for various models or configurations.

errors.text_span: Bars are presented in a single series, each corresponding to a language family and colored in shades of teal and purple.
errors.evidence: The bars are grouped by model/configuration (mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, etc.) and colored light blue, dark blue, light green, dark green, pink, and red, not a single series in teal and purple.

errors.text_span: The vertical axis is labeled 'effect' and represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at 5-unit intervals.
errors.evidence: The vertical axis range is 0 to 40, not 0 to 30.

errors.text_span: the Uralic bar is the tallest, reaching approximately 26
errors.evidence: The Uralic group has bars mostly below 5, not reaching 26.

errors.text_span: The IE-Baltic bar is the shortest, measuring approximately 2
errors.evidence: IE-Baltic bars range approximately from 2 to 7, not a single bar at 2. Also, the shortest bars are in the Uralic family.

errors.text_span: The IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Slavic, and Semitic bars all have similar heights around 14-16 units.
errors.evidence: IE-Indic bars range from 17 to 23, and Semitic bars range from -8 to 20, not all around 14-16.

errors.text_span: The IE-Romance bar measures approximately 20 units
errors.evidence: IE-Romance bars range approximately from 2 to 10, not a single bar at 20.
The description omits the six distinct models/configurations (mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, etc.) and their specific colors.
The description does not mention the grouped bar arrangement, which is critical for understanding the chart structure.
The description omits the tick interval of 5 units, though it is mentioned indirectly.
The language families are not listed alphabetically; their order is IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, etc.

errors.text_span: Bars are presented in a single series, each corresponding to a language family and colored in shades of teal and purple.
errors.evidence: The description is ambiguous about the actual grouping and coloring of bars, which represent models/configurations, not language families.

errors.text_span: The IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Slavic, and Semitic bars all have similar heights around 14-16 units.
